correctness.rationale: Closedness and compact invertibility follow from the exact rank-one factorization T=(I+e1⊗u)D, u_j=1/j and (I+e1⊗u)^-1=I-(e1⊗u)/2. For alpha<1/2, the transformed coefficient v_alpha=(j^(alpha-1)) lies in ell-two, making the closed bijection (I+e1⊗v_alpha)D_alpha the graph closure. For alpha>=1/2, weighted trace capacity vanishes on every tail; explicit graph approximants prove the closure is graph(D_alpha)+({0}×C e1). An independent adjoint-domain calculation confirms exactly the one-dimensional defect. The canonical form projection and finite-section weighted Cauchy–Schwarz identities then prove the stated decomposition and logarithmic critical cost. Exact-rational finite tests supplement but do not replace these infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A naturally defined graph-trace perturbation of a diagonal unbounded operator has compact inverse and is initially a closed bijection. Under increasing positive compact post-smoothing, closability changes sharply at one half, with a one-dimensional closed-relation defect and an exact jump of the canonical regular quadratic form. The finite-section trace capacity identifies a logarithmic critical regime and two different power-law regimes. This complete phase classification supplies a concrete quantitative model for the interaction of graph norms, trace continuity and Lebesgue decomposition; it is not merely a normalization check or arbitrary finite table.
